utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No. No. It's written here. Families of military invalids and those who lost somebody in the war, who lost a family member in the war. It says families of fighting men and Sehid, meaning victims' families.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Were you compensated or were you given an award for your own injury or for the fact that your son had died?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: There were many civilians who applied for some sort of indemnity, and there were two doctors who made a makeshift board, and they assessed disability, level of disability. They wrote 70 per cent for some people, 20 per cent for other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've raised a question one of my colleagues will pursue it, so I certainly won't take it any further. Your Honour, like Mr. Praljak, my client Mr. Petkovic may have one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to take a break because we are already late. We are using a lot of time. Mr. Karnavas maybe will not have any questions. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I do have about -- I would say three or four minutes. I will be very brief. It will summarise more or less what needs to be summarised, but I don't think I will take much more than five minutes if that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Nozica?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As it looks now, I will have one or perhaps two questions. Two or three minutes. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Very short, a couple of minutes only.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A couple of minutes perhaps, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will continue at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have no further questions myself, but as I indicated, Mr. Petkovic would like to ask a couple of questions, please. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good morning. Cross-examination by the Accused Petkovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. You can hear me I see. In 1993, were you 48 years old?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I was born in 1945, so you can work it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. You were 48 then. Now, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, if you were 48, are you still a military recruit?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't, but I could have been called up I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You are a 20 per cent invalid. May we have the following document on our screens, please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker repeat the number, please. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] P 08756 is the number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the document in front of you? It was from the military commission.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You have it on the screen in front of you, to speed things up. Can you see that? Take a look at the right, and it says "Form number 1." Have you read that?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Under that it says: "Military disability."

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you received a certificate saying that you were a 20 per cent military disability invalid; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it says that I was given it because of the family members of the Sehid or martyrs, victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It says that the families are entitled to that.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No. That was a different decision that I got for my son, but I don't receive anything on the basis of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But you have 20 per cent invalidity, disability 20 per cent; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's go back to IC 00277, please. And while we're waiting for the photograph to appear, I'm going to ask you the following -- can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: IC 00277. That is the place. That's the spot where he was wounded -- or, rather, where he was given assistance, helped later. That doesn't seem to be the right photograph. It is the house where he was taken in, where he was wounded. That's it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You say you were running across; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I was running across until halfway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did you run straight up or were you bowed down?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I suppose I was upright. Maybe I'd bent down a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, where you made the mark, that is where you were helped?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: They brought the stretcher in there and placed you on the stretcher, and then you were taken to hospital?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Would you take your pencil and indicate the path you took towards the hospital?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: The same route. Can you put the picture up a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did you take the route to the left passing by the house?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I went in the direction where I was wounded. The same way. I went and came back the same way, and down at the end of the path there was a vehicle waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And nobody shot at you there?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then how do you claim that when somebody is wounded they shoot at them? How many people carried you?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Nobody was shooting, but there were several people. I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So 15 minutes later you returned to the same spot on the way back and nobody shot at you?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly be asked not to overlap. Thank you. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next counsel. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examination by Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic:

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to remind the witness of a Prosecution document. P 08170 is the number, and it will come up on our screens. It is the certificate relating to your son, saying that he died as a fighter. P 08170. The date is 1994, the certificate, and I assume that you received your rights on the basis of the certificate issued on the death of your son. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Right. And on the basis of that certificate, as the mother and father of the person who was killed, you were given your rights?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I asked for this when I went to be ensured on the basis of what my doctor said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And you were granted certain rights?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And if you allow me --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Never mind. That's all I wanted to ask you. Thank you. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We're going to make pauses, otherwise we overlap and nobody can hear us. Next document P 08716. It's the document we looked at a moment ago. P 08756 [as interpreted]. It is the findings. Now, if I understood it correctly, in 1997 you tried to get some rights and remuneration for having been wounded yourself.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, everybody got something, so I thought I could ask for something, too, as a civilian victim, but I wasn't able to get anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It is P 08716. So you went before this military commission, and in point 4 on page 2, can we have a look at that, page 2, point 4, the findings. In point 4 it says at the top that it was ascertained that the military disability amounted to 20 per cent. It was permanent disability. And I assume that you didn't receive anything on the basis of that because 20 per cent is too little.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask for anything. I wasn't a soldier, so I didn't ask for anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But why did you go to this military commission?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Everybody did. All the civilians. Everybody did. They all went up before a commission like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, Mr. Dilberovic, kindly understand that you when you speak in your own tongue, language, that you cannot always overlap with the other speaker. You have to wait until the counsel finishes and then to start speaking only when everything is quiet. I hope that you will understand this. Thank you. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Dilberovic, to avoid this problem we're having in overlapping, I will give you a sign to start when I stop and when I see the interpretation has finished.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Just you go ahead. When you stop talking, I will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You have to count to five before you continue, all right? Count to five. Not out loud, of course. Now, when you went before the military commission, did you tell them you were a civilian?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say a thing. I didn't say anything. I just handed them the hospital document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. I have just have something brief to ask you. There were many witnesses in this courtroom before you who told us about the kind of uniforms that the soldiers had, the HVO soldiers and the BH army soldiers, et cetera, and the conclusion that we were able to draw up until now was that on that -- that the BH army wasn't very well equipped militarily speaking. Am I right? In that 1993 period. And they couldn't have been, of course.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, is it true and correct that at that time soldiers put on anything they had? Some had camouflage uniforms, others used the old olive-green uniforms or parts of those uniforms that the Yugoslav People's Army used to have. And we know there were grey ones, blue ones, olive-green ones and so on.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't go down there where they were, but I'm sure that there were all sorts of uniforms, but I can't say exactly what kind of uniforms they wore. I really don't know. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have no questions, but I would just like to clarify something that entered in -- that was put in the transcript, and that is that Pusic [as interpreted] -- the Pusic Defence counsel attended the visual representations. My client on the 1st of July, 1994 [as interpreted], was at a meeting where they discussed the technological aspects of these presentations. They were not an active participant in compiling the exhibits when the visual presentation was shown. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a mistake in the transcript? It was 2004, not 1994. Page 54, line 8. Next counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I just have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First, let me begin by thanking you for coming here to give your evidence. Now, sir, as I understand it, from the testimony that we heard on that particular afternoon, there was shooting going on before you got hit; correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You could hear shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the shots that you were hearing were coming from both directions. In other words, from east to west and from west to east?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I heard a shot. I heard shooting, but where I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I am -- I never heard that -- the witness say that the shots came from two directions. You said they went west/east and east/west. He never said that, so I was rather startled when you said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you should be startled, Your Honour, because this is cross-examination. I'm trying to get the witness to tell me whether that happened. He said shots. Where did the shots come from? They could have come from north to south, south to east, east to west. I don't know. That's what I'm trying to get from the gentleman. The whole point is that he heard shooting. Now, where was that shooting? So I am trying to clarify this. This is classic cross-examination, one step at a time, declarative statements. The gentleman can correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, sir, could you tell where the shots were coming from, whether they were strictly coming from east to west, from west to east or from both directions?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: The bullet that hit me came from the west. I can say that with full certainty. Now, as to the other shooting, if you hear automatic rifle shots or I don't know. I don't know who was shooting. You don't know who's shooting, where the shooting is coming from. All you do is run and try and flee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. So you do not -- you allow for the possibility, in fact, the probability, that there was shooting going from both directions?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Not then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm not talking about when you were shot.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The shot that came from you. The bullet that hit you. I'm talking about the shooting that preceded, because based on your testimony, there was shooting and you waited and then when there was some quiet that's when you ran across.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the -- those were the sniper shots that I heard, bullets I heard, and then I waited for the situation to calm down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you told us -- you showed us the general direction. You don't know with any degree of certainty where that shot came from?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... was a sniper --

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- or whether he was a huntsman or whether he was a sharpshooter or whether he was just a soldier or whether he was just an individual?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see anybody, so I can't say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the bullet, did they ever retrieve the bullet to examine the bullet so we know at least with some degree of certainty from what kind of weapon that came from?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No, no. No, they didn't. It went through my leg, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so you don't know what kind of weapon was used? You yourself.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: The shot came from a sniper. Now, how, I don't know. I know they shot from the western side from a sniper. Now, who did the shooting, I don't know. I don't know whether it was Muslim, Croat, Serb, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And you don't know whether that shot that hit you whether it had ricochetted from the ground and hit you or whether it was a direct shot?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. He -- he hit me directly in the leg, and it exited the other side. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you don't know the distance?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No. The people who -- well, they looked into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I understand it from your testimony, we saw you on a video with one individual, an investigator from the Prosecution, but you didn't meet an expert, a gunshot or sniping expert on that occasion to show him exactly what happened on the terrain on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, the people who came, we talked. We looked at the situation. Whether they were experts in that field or not I don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you heard the shot, the gunshot.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then -- and then based on what you heard, you're able to tell us from approximately what direction the bullet came from; correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said. The western side, that's where the bullet came from. Who did the shooting, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did you hear the shot before you got hit or did you get hit and then heard the shot? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No. When it hit me, I heard the sound of a bullet going off. Before that, you could hear sniper bullets here and there, shots here and there. I said that too and I said that we waited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But I'm just trying to get the -- I guess, I'm trying to figure out, did you hear the shot before it hit you or was it at the same moment or did the bullet hit you and then you heard the shot? Which of the three?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Oh, please. When the bullet hit me I heard the shot. How can I hear over there waiting to be shot?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, you said you never went down there where they were. That's was the testimony that you just gave with respect to the colours of uniform that the -- the soldiers were wearing.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: There were all sorts of uniforms. That's the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But your answer was, and it has nothing to do with the uniforms, but your answer was you never went down there where they were, meaning, you never associated yourself with the soldiers, wherever they were; correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. All I know is that they were at the separation line at Santic Street. The HVO on one side, the BH army on the other, and that's where there was shooting coming from both sides, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And the separation line was in front of you on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No. It was always in Santic Street. There wasn't a separation line where I was. It was down there at Santic Street all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in front of you or behind you? The Muslim fighters.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No. In front of me in Santic Street across the bridge. You have to cross the bridge, Tito's bridge, and that's where the lines were. On one side you had the Croats, on the other side you had the BH army. The Croatian Defence Council if you prefer that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's where you heard the shooting on that particular day? Prior to you getting shot.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't looking to see where the shooting was heard from. It might have been on this side or over there, but you could just hear sniper fire. I don't know who was doing the shooting or where it was. You could just hear firing coming from a sniper, sniping firing. And we waited for the situation to calm down so that I could cross the road. Now, that's when the bullet hit me. Whether it was intentional or not I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Precisely. That's my point. Thank you very much, sir. I appreciate you coming here?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I was shot. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Last counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You -- you said in your statement, and I think today, that after you were shot, you were in the hygienic institute in Mostar for five or six days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It's there in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And then you were taken in a car by UNPROFOR to Medjugorje?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks to them my leg was saved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And then from Medjugorje you were flown in a helicopter to the hospital in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A helicopter from Medjugorje to Zenica, to the hospital there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Now, Medjugorje was -- is on the west bank of Mostar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: So that area was under the control of the HVO at that time?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: But nonetheless you were able to get a helicopter flight to take you to the ABiH army hospital at Zenica?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: It's a civilian hospital up there. But UNPROFOR, they drove us. They saw to it all. UNPROFOR sorted the transportation and everything else. They were along with us right up to Medjugorje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Okay. And then, do you know who transported you from Medjugorje to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. There was some planes, helicopters. I don't know much. I was just lying on the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Karnavas, the last advocate who asked you questions, asked you about your being on the video that we saw this morning, an investigator from the Prosecution. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And he also asked you whether you had met an expert witness, actually, a Dutch military officer. It was actually a Dutch military officer called Lieutenant Van Der Weijden. Do you happen to remember whether you met that gentleman, Lieutenant Van Der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: There were many of them. I don't know them by name. I didn't ask. They were very nice to me and I told them of my own free will whatever I knew, but I don't know them by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Finally, when you were interviewed by the Prosecution and made your statement at the end of June in 2001, why did you tell the investigator that you had been shot after your son's funeral during June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: You know, all this happened as I was coming back from the cemetery, from visiting my son's grave. That's maybe how it happened. I said when I was coming back with my wife and Ms. Anita, who was a Croat, from the cemetery. It's only about the date. On the 12th of June, neither Ms. Anita nor my wife came with me. It happened on the 30th of August when we went together to my son's grave. Maybe it was my slip. Maybe somebody else's. I don't know exactly. But there are documents to show when I was shot, when I was in the hospital, how I was treated, when my son died, so I don't see any dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I understand that, but I suppose my question was simply why you had given that version of it to the investigators. You're saying that you were just mixed up about the date; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Maybe they asked me, "Where were you coming from? Were you visiting your son's grave?" And I said, "Yes," and maybe that's how that date came to be entered. I had no intention, and I corrected it immediately, as soon as I saw it, because I knew that I had said something without really thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You gave the investigator some details about your son's funeral, didn't you? You said that it was held about 4.00 to 5.00 in the evening. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the afternoon, probably around 5.00. I don't know. I didn't have a watch. I know it was already close to nightfall. There was no shooting when I was burying my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Then later in your statement on page 3 of the English version you said this. I want to read this to you and ask you to listen, please. "Usually I would only cross this place early in the morning or late in the evening, but because of the funeral, I had to cross at this time." Do you remember saying that to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I said that I went to attend the funeral of my son with his mother who wanted to go on the 30th of August. That's correct. And as for the rest, I can't tell you, because I was wounded on the 30th of August, because that was the day when my wife had expressed her wish to go there. If I hadn't taken her there, she would have gone alone. I told her, "Okay. We are going." Ms. Anita, with whom we were very good neighbours, also wanted to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. So the explanation that you're giving to the Trial Chamber is that you simply got mixed up as between your son's funeral and a date some two months later when you went to visit your son's grave; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, because -- I don't know. I told you, my son was killed on the 12th of June. And it was written that on that occasion I went together with my wife and Ms. Anita. And it's true that I didn't go there with my wife on that occasion. I went with my wife on the 30th of August. That was her first visit to the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: But it was a mistake that you made, not a mistake that the investigator made when he was writing down what you said?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. If I made a mistake, I'm correcting it now because it's impossible. I have all the papers from the doctor to confirm when I was wounded. Maybe I did say that. I don't know whose mistake it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Mr. President. Thank you. Oh, if you just allow me a moment. I'm sorry. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just have one or two quick questions following up from the cross-examination if I might.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Dilberovic, you were asked a number of questions by the Defence concerning the entry and exit wounds you sustained. Can you tell it us, sir, what injury you suffered to your leg as a result of this gunshot wound?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: It's not an entry and exit wound. The doctors say it fractured the bone. An entry and exit wound is when it just enters and exits through the flesh, but I don't know how my wound is called properly in medical terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dilberovic. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just ask for one correction of the record. On page 63, line 14, it gives the impression that I was about to conduct a re-examination rather than Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, your evidence is complete now. I thank you on behalf of my colleagues and in my own name. And I now invite you to leave the courtroom escorted by the usher. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, we are now going to move into closed session. We should lower the blinds.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Witness, you will be referred to as Witness DB since you have been granted protective measures. And I'll first give a brief summary of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: (redacted). The witness was shot in the shoulder by a sniper while he was trying to assist a man named (redacted) who had been shot and wounded by a sniper. On another occasion, the witness was wounded by shrapnel while (redacted). The witness was also present when a colleague (redacted) was shot and killed by a sniper outside the (redacted) (redacted). Witness, I'm going to ask you a couple of questions about your statement. Is it correct that you provided a written statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 1st of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at the time you provided this written statement, did you answer the questions to the investigator truthfully?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I answered truthfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you answer the questions freely, that is, without any coercion?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Right. Of my own free will, without coercion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at the conclusion of the interview, sir, was your statement read back to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you then sign your statement in the English language?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If I could now provide the witness with a bundle of exhibits which includes his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at the first exhibit which is Exhibit 9858.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: This exhibit will be under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, could you go through this and is it correct that this is in fact the English and both -- and the Bosnian statement that are under this exhibit number that you provided in July 2001?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it correct that your signature is on the English version of the statement?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall that you met with an investigator and myself yesterday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at that meeting, do you remember that I asked you whether you had re-read your statement and whether you wanted to make any corrections to your statement?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it correct that you made the following corrections which are on the top page of paragraph -- the top paragraph of page 3 of the English statement and on the fifth paragraph of the B/C/S statement, page number 3? And I'll read out the corrections and you maybe can confirm it that that is indeed what you wanted to correct. That the sentence which reads: "A man called Refik Saric had been visiting us at the station and had been there for about an hour. Then he decided to leave." That this sentence is incorrect because "I never saw Refik Saric inside the fire brigade station that day and I do not know whether Refik Saric actually visited the station or not." Would that be one of the corrections that you wanted to make to the statement?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And was the other correction is that in -- in that same paragraph, the sentence which reads that you do not remember the exact date that you were shot at by the sniper is incorrect, because you know that the incident occurred on the 29th of September, 1993, as the injury that you sustained that day was recorded by the secretary of the fire station?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: That is another correction I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Is there anything else that you wish to add or correct to the written statement besides these two corrections?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you questions now about the subject matters contained in your written statement, would you answer -- answers reflect what is written in your statement with the exception of the two corrections that we just made?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I would like to tender the witness statement of Witness DB into evidence as Exhibit 09858.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, can you just briefly describe to the Court what happened to you on the 29th of September, 1993, when you were shot at?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: That morning at 10.00 or maybe 11.00 I was on the premises of the fire brigade, and I suddenly heard a cry. I ran towards the place where it came from, and I saw Mr. Saric. He was covered in blood. That's perhaps 20 metres away from the spot where I was before. I just ran to him, and I didn't manage to haul him around the corner because somebody already had done that. At the corner I felt a blunt strike in my right shoulder blade. I fell to my knees, and a second bullet passed just over my head and hit the wall. I managed to retreat around the corner, and I just sat there. A lady came up to me. She shrieked and cried, but she did not help me. I managed to get to the hospital. There was a policeman who helped me in. I found Mr. Saric there. I saw that his arm was covered in blood. The doctors were already taking him somewhere for a surgery, I suppose. And I saw my brother in the hospital as well. It turned out that it was my brother who had hauled Mr. Saric to the hospital. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Just one question to clarify, the rest is in your statement. But when you actually got out of the station in order to help Mr. -- Mr. Saric, was there any combat activity going on in that area at the time?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing. It was quiet at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like -- now like to move into private session, and I would like the witness to be shown a video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Murphy, take the time during the cross-examination unless you have a very substantive question, but I would be surprised if you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I just wondered whether Mr. Bos wanted to put on the record the results of his request to the witness to indicate certain things while we were in private session, just so there will be a permanent record of some kind of what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Just for the record, what you just indicated to us we'll need to have this on the record. Is it correct that when you indicated the entry wound you were pointing at the back of your shoulder and when you were indicating the exit wound you were pointing at the front of your right-hand shoulder; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood the opposite. Just a moment. Witness, the bullet entered in front or at the back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The bullet entered from the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I don't know if this is a translation problem or not, Your Honours, but I hope it's clear to everyone in the courtroom now. We'll have another exhibit which may, you know, make it even more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that when you met with an investigator and myself yesterday afternoon that you were also shown a 360-degree photograph, a photograph which can go all the way around?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it correct that this photograph was taken on the exact spot where you were shot at on the 29th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: At this point, I would like to show you this 360-degree photograph. Can you see it in front of -- in front of you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe in order to orient -- orient the people here in the courtroom, could you just tell us the direction this -- this photograph looks at? Is that -- which direction is that? Is that north, east, west, or south?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: This is towards the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to save time, Mr. Bos, two observations. We've already seen this photograph showed to another witness, and when the Judges were in Mostar we walked down this street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, what we'll do is we'll turn around the photograph, and what I would like you to do is to tell you to stop when you see the direction from where you believe that the shot that hit you in the back of your right-hand shoulder would have come from. And we'll just start turning the photograph around now.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, yesterday in proofing you stopped about the same moment and we made a video still of this -- of this part of the photograph, and I'm going to show you this video still here now in order ... Now, Witness, what I would like to ask you is whether you can indicate on this video still where you think the shot came from that -- that hit you on that day.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question. You've made a circle on this photograph right in the middle of the photograph, and there's a white house on the left of this circle. Was this white house there in 1993?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was, but part of the roof had been shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Witness, I have two more exhibits that I would like to show you, and they're in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A follow-up question. You've just indicated where the shot came from. We can't see very well, but there is a hill behind. Does that mean that in your opinion the person doing the shooting was up on the hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. They asked me that the first time, too, but I said I don't know. I'm not sure where the bullet came from, where the shooting came from, or the shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the shot came from the area where you drew the circle; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to now ask you to look at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Bos, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to look at Exhibit 7775, which is a medical record of a person that -- that was also on --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Perhaps Your Honour, to save some time, it may be more practical to add an IC number on that photograph immediately before moving to another subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Registrar, let's have an IC number for the photograph that the circle was drawn on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be given Exhibit number IC 281, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kovacic, for drawing our attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe, Mr. Witness, you could put the initials DB in the right-hand corner of the photograph and today's date which is the 31st of January.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, again, could I ask you to look at Exhibit 775, and in particular the third page of -- this is a medical record from Mr. Saric, who was -- who was also hit on that day and whom you -- whom we also saw on the video. And we have a couple of medical documents on -- on this person, and I'm particularly interested in the third page of the B/C/S version and also the English version, which starts with a date 24/10/93. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it correct that it says that -- that it says "injured with a rifle bullet on 29 September 1993. The wounds near the lower elbow are healed. Movement with fingers are limited"? Is that what it reads?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it's in English here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But I would -- there's also a B/C/S version. I'm sorry, I thought you were looking at the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, for interrupting, but it would be very useful if we were to see the document on e-court. There are a number of documents there, medical documents which relate to the same person, some with a P, others without a P, and it will be easier to clarify some more legible than others.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I also wish to point out that the gentleman is doing the exact thing that Judge Trechsel criticised General Praljak for doing, that is, asking whether the document says what it says. So I just wish to point this out, because it appears that the Prosecution is doing exactly what the Defence tries to do, but there are no objections when they do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, there's -- there's still a follow-up question on this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, what is written here, does that confirm which -- with what you saw in the hospital when you met Mr. Saric with regard to the wound?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, could we now move to Exhibit 992 -- well, this is not in the bundle, but if the e-court could show the witness page -- this is Exhibit 9220, which is a bundle of photographs, and we need page number 16 of this exhibit on e-court, which is ERN 05016235. Your Honours, maybe in order to save time, I have photographs here and we can put them on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It would be better to put them on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If you could look first at photograph number 16. Well, there you go. It's also on the ELMO now. Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What does it depict?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: You can see the entrance wound on my shoulder. Well, not my shoulder but the place I was hit, underneath the right shoulder blade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If we could now move to the next photograph which is underneath that one. And can we move to the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have an IC number for the first photograph, Mr. Registrar, the entrance wound. The first photograph, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be given Exhibit number IC 282, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And an IC number for the exit wound. The one we have up on our screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... IC 283, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Just, Witness, what we see here on the photograph, what does this depict, this second photograph?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Each Defence team has 10 minutes. Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness, the part of your statement that you have withdrawn in the proofing session is this, just remind you, that a man called Refik Saric had been visiting us at the station, had been there for about an hour, then he decided to leave. He'd only been gone a few seconds. Now, I just want to point out to you that there are four points there. He had been visiting the station. He had been there for about an hour. He decided to leave. He'd only been gone a few seconds before the incident that you then describe. How did you come to mistakenly give such a clear statement on four points and sign it in that statement, given that you now say it's not correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, please believe me when I say that a lot of time has gone by since then and I had forgotten a lot of things. I tried to forget them, did my best to. So I'd forgotten a lot of things at that time except for my own wounding. I never forgot that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stewart, for your information, the Appeals Chamber already dealt with this type of discrepancy and clearly indicated that it is possible that with the passage of time and the facts a witness can vary in what he says.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, perfectly correct, which is why we very often don't pick up such points, but as a general principle -- I leave it and move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Paragraph -- well, it's my paragraph 20. You also, when you signed the statement, said you had medical records for your injuries but at that time said, "I have no idea where they are." Had you lost them, mislaid them before you were ever interviewed by anybody connected with this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I never had those documents in my hands, in my possession, and that's why I said what I did. That's why I told the investigators that I had no papers in that connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Have you ever made any attempt to get hold of any medical records?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to the incident then. You -- you say you heard someone screaming. You went looking. You saw Saric standing hunched over. "I could see that he was bleeding on the hand where he had been hit by a sniper." At that point, you had no idea at all, did you, whether he had been hit by a sniper or not?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: No. I just heard the scream, the moan, and it was only when I got outside that I saw what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then you describe -- of course he'd already been shot. You described yourself being shot, and then you refer to another shot that you say was fired at you, went over your head and hit a wall. So three shots. Have any of those three bullets, as we must assume they are, ever been recovered?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Was any search ever undertaken on the day or any other time that you're aware of for those bullets?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, you made the correction to your statement that I asked you about a few minutes ago but can I be absolutely clear? Apart from the date which you corrected and apart from the business of Mr. Saric visiting the station, you stand by every single word in your statement, do you?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In your statement you were asked apparently, specifically, in terms -- and you were talking about the person that shot you, you said, "I have no idea where the sniper had fired his bullets from." So can we take it that, although you've been shown photographs this morning and although you've indicated possibilities, it remains the position that you personally simply have no idea where the shot came from?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I think it was in 2004, that I wasn't sure where the bullet came from or who did the firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In your statement you also refer to another incident relating to -- are we -- well, another incident. Do you know -- I'm just not entirely comfortable, Your Honour, whether I should say the name. We're in open session. I don't want the witness to be under any misunderstanding what it is. Do you remember you referred to an incident much later where a tanker was parked on the pavement outside the station, same street but much later on. And then you say there'd been a few rifle shots, and this is a colleague of yours that unhappily died. Do you know which incident I'm talking about, do you?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. And you said there that there had been -- you had been -- the tanker was parked on the pavement. You were at work apparently. You said there had been a few rifle shots and then I heard him say he was shot. "I went outside and we couldn't see him straight away." Over what period did those rifle shots occur? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question fully. Can you repeat it? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'll move on. You went outside, then, when you heard the shot. You were engaged weren't you straight away of course in trying to help, immediately help your unfortunate colleague and get him out of harm's way and get him to hospital. That was your priority task wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You didn't, yourself, conduct any inspection at all of the wound. You just saw it was a very unpleasant wound. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, my last question probably, depending on the answer. My last question: You say that the area where you were shot was not normally a dangerous place to be. This is your statement. You've not seen snipers firing there before. "I didn't see them firing there afterwards." So it follows that whatever the location from which this sniper fired at you, you say it was a sniper, whatever the location from where that shot was fired, you personally have no knowledge of that location ever having been used before for firing or ever being used afterwards. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next Defence team. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no questions for this witness, and we have given our time to the Praljak Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have also placed our time at the disposal of the Praljak Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President. Thank you very much. We wish to thank the gentleman for coming here to give his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: We have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, General Praljak has expressed the wish to ask a few questions to start off with, and I might have a few at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Just a moment, please. The Judges have a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, my question follows on from what Mr. Stewart was asking you. The spot, the location where the incident took place wasn't dangerous but did it become dangerous afterwards? After you and your colleague were shot, were there other incidents that took place in the same spot? That's my first question. And, secondly, did the shots target people from coming out of the place you were in, from the fire station there 15 metres away, did they consistently target people coming out of that building, those premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, the sniper didn't shoot at that spot at all. Up until that day when Mr. Saric and I, myself, were hit. After that, another man was shot nearby. I don't know the name. Do I need to say the name in open session? Can I say the name? Afterwards there were no other incidents, no other shooting or anything. Beforehand, that wasn't a dangerous place. It wasn't targeted ever before. We passed by that way very often and it was never targeted until that particular day. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I can't use your name, so I'll just say good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We're very simply going to go through a number of photographs which were taken from different positions round that location. You are an inhabitant of Mostar, a local. I'm sure you know the situation very well. I do up to a point too. So may we have those photographs placed on the overhead projector and we'll take them one by one. Once the photographs are on the ELMO, I'll continue. That is the first photograph, and you'll agree with me, or not agree with me, when I say that this photograph was taken from the corner of Brkic and Marsal Tito Street, the right corner if you're looking westward?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And as the previous photograph showed, that's the spot where you were wounded.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, would you take up the marker pen handed to you by the usher and put a cross where that was.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Let me just make this clear. I was further up. Not that position. You mean where I was wounded? It wasn't here. It was further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the next photograph. Can we have the next photograph on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: That's not as good either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Let's go back to the first photograph. Just show us where the fire brigade was, the fire station. And you can put a number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. It's behind the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Right. Behind the wall. You can put an arrow showing the entrance into the fire station.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Would you now, roughly, and we saw this on the previous photograph, mark the distance from the wall, the place where you were wounded. Is that halfway between the street and the wall, nearer the wall? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: It was a little closer to the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Put down DB, please, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we see the next photograph now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: This is taken from a similar spot, and we see to the left the Hasan Brkic Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Can you mark it with 1.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: You mean Neretva Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can we have an IC number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm looking at this photo. You've just marked Neretva Hotel. I wonder, if there was a sharpshooter in the hotel, how come that you were shot in the spot where you were shot? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have no explanation. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I will ask you further. Was the Neretva Hotel torched when the Serbs were on the right bank of the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Was the Neretva Hotel on the left bank of the Neretva River?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So it was on the left bank. At the time when you were wounded, was that hotel on the left bank under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next photo, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a number? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can you place your initials at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: IC number 285, Your Honours. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's the same photograph. Do we see again Hotel Neretva in the distance?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Can you mark it with 1?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And initials DB.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And that's on the right side, the entrance to the fire station.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Place a arrow and number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: IC number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken from such an angle as to show Marsal Tito Street, the pavement where you were injured, and the corner of Hasan Brkic street.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Tell me, where did the bullet hit, the second bullet?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The wall; right? Put a number 1.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And to the right. That's the road that goes up. A larger arrow.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be given Exhibit number IC 287, Your Honours. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next photograph, please. Turn it around.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sir, this is something that we see from the west side of Mostar and the west bank of Neretva. We look across the Marsal Tito bridge at Musala and the Hasan Brkic street; correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Was Marsal Tito bridge destroyed in 1992 in May by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: On the right side, is there something that the people of Mostar call Banja?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: On the right side behind Banja, is that the music school?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Further in the distance below the mosque was a travel agent, Putnik. Mark it, please.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, along the road as we go across the Marsal Tito Street, if you go to the left you enter Hasan Brkic street. Can you mark that route.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Show us the bend and then -- right. That's it.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So that is number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now just tell me one more thing. At the time when the Yugoslav People's Army and its reservists came to Mostar, was Banja burned down?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Was the music school destroyed and burned down?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Hotel Neretva?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The travel agent Putnik, were they burned down?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. Place your initials there, please.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] And can I have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be given Exhibit number IC 288, Your Honours. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: This is the same thing closer up. Please show us how you enter Hasan Brkic street, again going across the bridge and taking the same route.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Follow the road. Follow the road. The road is to the left, more to the left. That's it.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, what we see here is the music academy; correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: IC 289, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Place number 2 on the music academy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. Next photograph, please. We're now looking from the opposite side, from the east side to the west side, and we'll take it again one by one. This dilapidated building, is that the Neretva Hotel?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Please mark it with a 1.

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: On the left side, is that Banja?

utterances.speaker: OMER DILBEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
